name: Mixed Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Mixed Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of chronic systemic inflammation with elevated acute phase reactants
Clinical or serological evidence of autoimmune phenomena (e.g., autoantibodies, organ-specific autoimmunity)
Recurrent or periodic fever episodes without infectious cause
Exclusion of other defined autoinflammatory or autoimmune diseases
Identification of mutations or variants in genes associated with autoinflammatory and autoimmune pathways

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic systemic inflammation plus autoimmune features and exclusion of other defined diseases
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by laboratory and genetic findings; no universally accepted criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent febrile episodes with elevated C-reactive protein
searchTerms: frequent fever episodes with raised CRP

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of multiple autoantibodies (e.g., ANA, anti-dsDNA)
searchTerms: presence of ANA and anti-dsDNA antibodies

common.symptomName: Chronic fatigue related to systemic inflammation
searchTerms: chronic fatigue due to systemic inflammation

common.symptomName: Interstitial lung disease with restrictive pattern

occasional.symptomName: Renal involvement with proteinuria and hematuria
searchTerms: kidney problems with protein and blood in urine
lymph node swelling with reactive changes
low platelet count from immune attack

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
Positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and other autoantibodies
imaging: Interstitial lung changes on high-resolution CT
Cardiac MRI showing myocarditis in rare cases
genetic: Variants in genes involved in inflammasome regulation (e.g., NLRP3, MEFV)
other: Histopathology showing mixed inflammatory infiltrates in affected tissues
Response to immunomodulatory therapy supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent autoantibody profile without recurrent fever episodes
Characteristic malar rash and renal lupus nephritis
Predominantly autoinflammatory with episodic fever and serositis

redFlags: Severe refractory systemic inflammation despite treatment
Development of life-threatening organ involvement (e.g., myocarditis)
references: Federici S, et al. Mixed autoinflammatory and autoimmune syndromes: clinical features and genetic insights. Autoimmun Rev. 2022;21(5):102987.
